newsitem.title: MACAU: Charges filed in Macau attack on Chinese envoy.
newsitem.headline: Charges filed in Macau attack on Chinese envoy.

text.p: A Macau court on Saturday charged two men and a woman in relation to an attack on a Chinese diplomat and his driver in the Portuguese-administered territory, court officials said.
The three were charged with causing bodily harm and released on 3,000 patacas (US$375) bail each, the court heard. They were also ordered to surrender their travel documents, court officials said.

The second secretary of China's delegation of the Sino-Portuguese Joint Liaison Group (JLG) -- which will oversee Portugal's handover of Macau to Chinese rule in 1999 -- and his driver were attacked with iron bars on Friday morning.
The incident occured in front of a building housing mainland Chinese officials posted to Macau. On Sunday, the two men were still recovering in hospital in satisfactory condition.

Macau police said on Sunday they were still looking for several suspects in connection with the assault. A police source said the attackers were likely low-ranking gangsters connected to local organised crime syndicates known as triads.
